trickyParts: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is read for the chosen-title reader through configuredValue, not through pluginStateDirectory(): that helper throws when the variable is unset and is deliberately called after the Envoy-off early return, so reusing or moving it would turn a session with Envoy off and no plugin data into a crash.

readChosenTitleSync is synchronous and swallows every error on purpose. The registration path reads it inside a (sessionId) => string, and the title is cosmetic: a failed read must leave the session on its fallback name rather than fail the registration that carries it.

The new UserPromptSubmit hook must stay silent on stdout and exit 0 whatever happens, malformed input included, because Claude Code adds such a hook's stdout to the model's context and reads its exit code 2 as a block of the user's prompt. The dispatcher in hooks/session-hook.ts was restructured so this mode's JSON.parse is inside its own guard while the two older modes keep failing loudly on a payload that is not JSON.

The hook writes the chosen name untrimmed and uncleaned; src/session-title.ts's existing oneLine/visible pair is the one place that cleans and judges it, so a blank, invisible or multi-line name falls through to the fallback by the same rule every other source follows.

An agent row's heading no longer uses TruncatedText at all: the component exists for text that ellipsises inside a flex container, and this name never does. packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md's list of its hosts was corrected accordingly.

openQuestions: Plan A4, reported rather than asserted, as the architect accepted on 2026-10-24T23:22:06Z: a Legion Claude pane's name lands on its first prompt, not at launch. The daemon seeds a fresh pane with '/rename Legion <role> · <KEY>' as a user message (packages/daemon/internal/claudebridge/bridge.go:196-199), so the UserPromptSubmit hook sees the custom title on the pane's next prompt — the daemon's first task — and the pane reads as 'Legion implementer · INFRA-92' from then on. That a slash command arriving on stream-json input renames the session is Claude Code's own behaviour, which no test here covers and no pod here can run.

Plan decision 9, unchanged behaviour recorded so the next phase does not read it as a regression: a session whose Envoy or inbound messages are off registers nothing, so it stamps its title once at startup and a later rename does not reach its Dispatch attribution. That is today's behaviour for every title and is not this change's to fix.
